clue.text: They are for checking on beatings

definitions.text: They are for checking on beatings

parts.words: They are for checking on beatings
parts.note: beatings here are heartbeats, which a doctor listens to and checks, not thrashings

explanation.surface: Someone describing the instruments used to monitor punishments being handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beatings' suggests violence, but the beats are those of the heart, checked by a doctor's listening tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's listening instruments are used to check the heartbeat, so they check on beatings.

clue.text: The casual worker has to move briskly

definitions.meaning: one who scamps, doing work carelessly or skimpily

explanation.walkthrough: To scamp is to do work carelessly, so one who does so is a careless or casual worker; 'casual' here means slapdash, not temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamp a job is to skimp it, so one who scamps is slapdash; the verb also means scurry.

clue.text: A diplomatic retreat

parts.note: a tactful withdrawal, or else a refuge run by diplomats where people may take shelter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomatic retreat' suggests a tactful backing down; read literally it is a place where diplomats work and refugees may seek asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official residence can serve as a refuge where asylum seekers retreat.

clue.text: Wild hounds bark here in America

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the word hounds runs riot into a new order

parts.note: to bay is to bark or howl, as hounds do

explanation.surface: Untamed dogs barking somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges HOUNDS into HUDSON. The bay is in north-eastern Canada, part of North America.
explanation.definitionFit: This large inland sea lies in Canada, on the North American continent, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: Bearing with insubstantial rising in the country

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so from bottom to top

parts.note: airy means light and insubstantial

explanation.surface: A flimsy rebellion breaks out somewhere in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns AIRY into YRIA. 'Rising' suggests an uprising, but it is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation of the Middle East, so it is a country.

clue.text: It's best to decide on one without speaking

parts.note: to opt is to choose or decide
I is the Roman numeral one
mum means silent, as in keep mum

explanation.surface: It's wisest to make one's choice silently.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable outcome or level, the best possible.

clue.text: Beg in the town-centre a tramp's way of life

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these clue words

explanation.surface: A vagrant's life is begging in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'town-centre a tramp's'; 'the' and 'way of life' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or implore earnestly, a synonym of beg.

clue.text: Capital work he does in the theatre

definitions.text: Capital work he does in the theatre

parts.words: Capital work he does in the theatre
parts.note: capital is used in its sense of relating to the head, and the theatre is an operating theatre, not a stage

explanation.surface: Praise for an actor's excellent stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like 'excellent' and 'theatre' a playhouse; really it is head work in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist surgeon operates on the head, in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Not a berth in a caravan though it supports sleepers

definitions.text: Not a berth in a caravan though it supports sleepers

parts.words: Not a berth in a caravan though it supports sleepers
parts.note: the phrase looks like a bed on the road, as in a caravan, but the sleepers are the wooden railway ties laid on ballast

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where people sleep when travelling by caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepers are the cross-ties of a railway track; the foundation layer beneath a railway or road carries them. A caravan's bunk would be a 'road bed' in the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The foundation layer under a railway track is what the cross-ties rest on, so it supports sleepers.

clue.text: A roundabout device, however one may regard it

indicators.note: the word reads the same from either direction, whichever way one looks at it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A gadget for going round in circles, described from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part or mechanism turns round, so it is a roundabout device.

clue.text: In the matter of louts, sense new determination

parts.note: re means concerning, in the matter of

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Concerning hooligans, a fresh sense of firm purpose is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LOUTS and SENSE into SOLUTENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being firmly purposeful and unwavering is resolve, which is determination.

clue.text: The artist's laying it on thick

definitions.text: The artist's laying it on thick

parts.words: The artist's laying it on thick
parts.note: laying it on thick usually means exaggerating, but here a painter literally applies paint in a heavy layer

explanation.surface: A painter who is flattering or exaggerating heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying it on thick' sounds like flattery; read literally, it is the technique of applying paint thickly to a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: This painting technique applies pigment in thick layers that stand out from the canvas.

clue.text: 'ardly descriptive of many clubs without members?

definitions.meaning: with the dropped H of Cockney speech, harmless becomes this word; clubs as weapons are hardly harmless
having no arms, the limbs called members

explanation.surface: A remark that many sports clubs lack members, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''ardly' signals Cockney speech, in which 'harmless' loses its H. Clubs here are cudgels, and members are limbs, not people who join a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Members can mean limbs, and the word means lacking arms; a cudgel is hardly free of harm.

clue.text: Branch appears active, accepting small article

indicators.note: the word for active takes in the article, holding it inside itself

parts.note: spry means lively and active
a is the indefinite article, a short word

explanation.surface: A branch of a business seems busy and is taking in a minor item.
explanation.definitionFit: A small twig or shoot with leaves or flowers is a spray, a kind of branch.

clue.text: Teams able to slip into lead for instance

indicators.note: the letters of these two words slip out of place and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Sports teams are able to slip into the lead in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as being ahead in a contest; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a common, non-precious metal, as opposed to gold or silver.

clue.text: Ask a higher price for fish caught in swell

indicators.note: the fish is trapped inside the word for swell, like a catch in the sea

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: A fishmonger charging more for fish caught in a heavy sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy an extra charge on something is to ask more than the normal price.

clue.text: Local council supporter fined for speeding?

definitions.text: Local council supporter fined for speeding?

parts.words: Local council supporter fined for speeding?
parts.note: someone who pays local property taxes to the council, jokingly read as one who pays for exceeding a speed rate

explanation.surface: A council's backer who got a ticket for driving too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British local property tax funding councils; the joke reads 'rate' as speed, so the payer pays for going too fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A householder paying local property taxes funds, and so supports, the local council.

clue.text: A great blow to the Chinese

definitions.text: A great blow to the Chinese

parts.words: A great blow to the Chinese
parts.note: a blow suggests a disaster, but here it is a huge wind storm of the China seas

explanation.surface: A news line about a serious setback for China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' reads as a setback; it is a strong wind, a tropical storm of the western Pacific, a word believed to come from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent tropical cyclone of the western Pacific is a great wind, or blow.

clue.text: River bird tucked into by a furtive fellow

indicators.note: the river and bird letters are tucked inside the word for by

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
R is the map abbreviation for river
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A sneaky character eats a river fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sneaks around stealthily, looking for a chance to steal, is a furtive person.

clue.text: Take up exercise after some trouble

indicators.note: the exercise abbreviation comes after the word for fuss

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone taking up exercise after a spell of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or plan is to take it up as one's own.

clue.text: Only a seaman gets sea-ear

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
alone means only, as in he alone knew

explanation.surface: A lone sailor acquires an unusual shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea-ear is a large edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-ear is another name for this edible mollusc, from its ear-like shell.

clue.text: Mail dispatched to a station in the wilds?

parts.note: out means sent away, as of letters dispatched
post is mail

explanation.surface: Letters are sent off to a remote station.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote settlement or garrison far from civilisation is a station in wild country.

clue.text: Former page learning to investigate

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
lore is knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A former pageboy uses his learning to look into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore a matter is to look into it thoroughly, a synonym of probing.

clue.text: Oriental cape turning up in a German place

parts.note: E is east, the Orient

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: An Eastern cloak appears in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses NESS to SSEN. Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, a location in Germany.

clue.text: Encourage to listen in before ten

parts.note: to hear is to listen in

explanation.surface: Urging someone to tune in before ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to cheer and embolden them.

clue.text: Fools are soon led astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Gullible people are quickly misled.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles is an informal word for simpletons or silly people.

clue.text: Taking port to America — it's not controlled

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Shipping a port's goods to America is unregulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous behaviour is wild and unrestrained, beyond any control.

clue.text: Possibly ten managed to stick together, which is fascinating

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be put in another order

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
to cement is to bind or stick together

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten people managed to stay united, which is captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN into ENT. 'Fascinating' is here a noun, the act of holding someone spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascinating someone, as a noun of action, is holding them spellbound, which is a trance-like enchantment.
